I had the opportunity of seeing this man when he went for work obligation. A few times he succeeded in giving us a sandwich or something, so we would share this among ourselves. He had work obligation at Master.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am only interested in whether you know that other fellow citizens of yours had work obligation in Bosanski Samac or in other institutions. Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everybody. All Muslims and Croats had forced work obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that because they worked in these enterprises, you did not see them there where you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Many times when I would be taken to a different location, I would not have the possibility of seeing all my fellow citizens when they were working at other facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell me, sir: A while ago, today, this morning, in response to the Prosecutor's question that had to [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, could you just pause before you answer. I don't even manage to switch off the microphone, and the interpreters should also be assisted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Do you know that in line with the law on abandoned property, the tenants of such shops are duty-bound to pay rent to the municipality? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. I don't know. I considered things like that to be robbery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "robbery." Did anybody ever take away your ownership over this shop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as soon as I was detained and exchanged. On several occasions I was told, "What have you got to do in Bosanski Samac?" Or to be more precise, in Serb Samac. "You are here. You have nothing any more. Don't you know that this is Serb land?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In documents concerning [redacted] and the ownership of [redacted] [redacted], ever over these ten years was anybody else's name put in there instead of [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have this before me. However, if I am the owner of something, no one can transfer this to someone else's name without my consent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I absolutely agree with you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why are you putting this kind of question to me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to clarify some facts. You answered my previous question by saying that you did not know about rent being paid to the municipality for the use of your shop; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. And I would wonder where this money went. I would wonder whether a single shop or house was taken away from anyone of Serb background. I would wonder whether all of that which was taken away was returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are certainly aware of the fact that this happened all happened over Bosnia-Herzegovina and Sarajevo and elsewhere; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I felt this on my very own skin quite pronouncedly. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]. Buildings were made, and many participants in this courtroom here live in these apartments [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, you are talking about the time before the 17th of April, 1992, and we here are not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's when we were the owners of that. After the 17th, in 1992, I would like to erase all of that, all of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I have a question, actually for yourself, Mr. Zecevic. You were saying that where there were abandoned buildings, the tenants, so I presume new tenants, [redacted] [redacted]--

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: -- would pay rent to the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So what I would like to know is, obviously being unfamiliar with the municipal law there --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: -- what did the municipality do with that money that was paid in rent?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I really can't answer that question, because I don't know what has been done, but during our case we will present the proof that these funds have been under the control of the municipality, and as far as I know, the previous owners, or the real owners, are entitled to ask from the municipality reimbursement of all the rent which was paid to the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's just clarify something. You were talking about these buildings, about the property that your ancestors had in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You thought that this was taken -- you meant that this was taken away from you during the communist regime, right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the meantime, was somebody else the owner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me whether I know that this could be given to someone else, handed over to someone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just understand each other clearly. There is ownership and there is use. You are the owner but it was used by somebody else because you were not in Bosanski Samac, as we know; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not get my personal documents either, let alone documents about ownership over something that I had. So I was kicked out of my own town. I did not get any documents where it said that I was the owner of something. I did not have the possibility of getting my personal ID, and I own that too. Even that was taken away from me. And I only had a card that was issued to me by the Red Cross, the International Red Cross with its seat in Geneva. There was a number on it and a name and a surname, no picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, what is the exact thrust of your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: And then in the year 2000, after he came back, he repossessed; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He repossessed it. Exactly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: So what is the question between 1992 and 2000 now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the point, Your Honour, is that his ownership was undisputed all this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: His ownership is undisputed. The possession is the other thing. That was the only question that I wanted to ask him, whether [redacted]. That was the only thing I wanted to ask. And he said -- I mean, the witness was explaining other things. I just wanted that answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: -- and the question possibly to ask is: "Did you rent it out? Did you give permission to anybody to use it while you were in detention?" That is the first question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. Exactly, Your Honours, but he answered that question that no rent was paid to him and that he never rented [redacted], while he was examined-in-chief this morning. So I didn't want to repeat myself again. So I know that he didn't rent it on his own will, and he never received the rent. I'm just trying to focus on the ownership, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: So what is the question? Because he has said that he was the owner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I would like the witness to answer if he knows whether somebody else was, in the meantime, from 1992 until 2001, if somebody else -- was somebody else listed in the books as the owner, so that his ownership was taken away from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You must frame the question clearly to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am trying my best, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope you've understood what the point of my question is. Do you know that between 1992 and the year 2000, when this [redacted] was returned to you, that anybody else's name was in any kind of document as the owner instead of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I would like to ask the witness a question if I could. Questioned by the Court: It would appear from my question to counsel a few minutes ago that for the period that someone was renting your property, between 1992 and the year 2000, that rent would have been paid to the municipality in your town, and it would appear from what we've heard that you would be entitled to go to the municipality in Bosanski Samac and seek compensation for that period, 1992 to 2000. I have two questions for you, Witness. The first is: Were you aware -- are you aware that you're entitled to compensation? And secondly: If you are aware, have you actually, since being back there in your town, have you made a request for compensation and received it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, I hope that you've put this question to me. I have been there for 13 months now. During those 13 months, I went to various institutions with the request to bring electricity back to my house. Everything that I had to do, starting with the electricity meter to the switches, nobody wanted to give me a thing. [redacted] [redacted]. I have always been given the following answer: that I should find the thief, either by myself or with the assistance of the police of Bosanski Samac, and then that they would prosecute the person who took away my equipment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] had to pay for that pole before the war so that we could get electricity. I said, "People, there was an electricity pole here before." And they said, "Well, it's not there, and if you want electricity, you will have to pay for this pole again and to pay for power being brought [redacted]." When I realised where I came back, when I rented out [redacted] to a gentleman of Serb ethnicity, I asked him that he ask for electricity to be returned and that he asked for some kind of compensation. In that case, he did get electricity back within two days. And I paid myself for [redacted], and I put in a few electric switches. And now he is paying rent to me on a regular basis. I did not have the money [redacted]. Wherever I would get, I would have to start with electricity. And then I thought perhaps somebody would give me some other material or some equipment, but I did not meet with any understanding from the commander of the police station to the manager of the power supply company. And the International Red Cross is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness. My question was directed solely to the issue of the rent that was being paid, the money that was being paid to the municipality and so on. If you could just address that. First of all, did you go, have you been to whatever the official municipal offices are in Bosanski Samac to seek money back for the rent that was paid by whoever was the tenant? Could you answer that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to ask for that. I didn't even know about these regulations. Not a single citizen of Muslim or Croat ethnicity who returned did get any compensation for the use of either business premises or a house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just a follow-up there. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [redacted]. And from our own savings that we saved up from our salaries, we created this. And we created this new workplace for her. And this was her new workplace until the 17th of April, 1992, until this was taken away and until all the goods were taken away. All of it was plundered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: My simple question is: After -- just before 17th of April, did you -- did you rent this premises out to anybody else? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Singh, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: , and did he have your permission to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person did not have any permission. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we warned her, saying that she was in this facility illegally, without our permission, she answered us over the phone, "What do you want? Do you know that this is Republika Srpska?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Now, the last question: Did you go to the municipality and find out if she had been paying rent to the municipality, rent which was in fact due to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did not check this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let's go back to the period immediately before the 17th of April, 1992. As you told us here, you possessed this semi-automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, until the 17th of April [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday during the examination-in-chief, you said that you do not remember who gave you this weapon in the TO building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 30th of August, you gave a statement to the Prosecution, 1998. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did give them a statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a statement on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would the usher please assist me. I would like to present this statement to the witness. It's the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor on 30th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just show it to the witness so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The witness said that he had owned or possessed the weapon until "17 hours," and not until the "17th of April." Page 59, line 4 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It states here my name, my surname, date of birth, the year of birth, and the place of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see that it says here as the date of the interview as the 30th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, the 30th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the last page? There is a confirmation of your signature there, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here, "Witness acknowledgement."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This is one of the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. I was directed there is a problem with -- please bear with me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a problem. We will go back to your statement. A little while ago when I asked you about the weapon, the gun, you said that you had it in your possession for a total of 17 hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for about 17 hours. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the moment you took it until the moment you gave it back; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know. The municipality of Srpski Samac has better information. It is in possession of the proper documents, so that they will tell me, and probably, with their consent, we will arrive at the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I only asked you this so that we could clear up something in the transcript, because something else was written in the transcript. Thank you. This is your statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read it, but I hope it is my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not checking, but I will just see if it is really my statement. Yes, sir, Mr. Slobodan Zecevic, this is my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. A little while ago you said that you spoke with the Prosecutors on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions. Whether it's called "the Prosecutor" or "the Prosecution," I don't know, but it does say here "The International Criminal Tribunal for the Prosecution of persons responsible for serious violations of international law committed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia since 1991." MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting, but I just -- I'm a little unclear if the witness and Mr. Zecevic are talking about investigators or prosecutors, meaning lawyers from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The investigators, of course. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful. I wasn't clear about that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify something: You spoke with the investigators from the Prosecutor's office? Did you speak with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you for sure. I had contacts with many people after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is the only official statement that you gave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I gave many statements, in the press, in the media, and also these statements. I gave a statement as soon as I was released from the transporter of the UN on the 4th of October, 1992. Who they were, whether they were investigators or whether they were fellow citizens over there of my Sarajevo at that time, I really wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you kindly turn to page 4. MR. DI FAZIO: I wonder if Mr. Zecevic could tell us where in the English it is so that I could follow this portion of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is -- MR. DI FAZIO: Unfortunately, they're not numbered, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is the page number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's the fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's the page number 3, fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, would you be kind enough to read the fourth paragraph of this statement. It begins: "At 9.00 a.m. of the same morning..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please read it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That's what I wanted to clarify with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. I didn't understand that I was supposed to read it out loud. "At 9.00 a.m. the same morning, I heard Ibrahim Salkic speaking from a megaphone. From the megaphone, he asked all of those who were given arms at the TO to hand those weapons over to the Serbs and thus avoid further problems. I didn't know if he was captured at that time. He was one of the men who armed us at the TO. I surrendered my rifle to one member of the Serb paramilitary." If that is the passage that you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly the one that I meant. You indicated here that Ibrahim Salkic was one of the persons who gave you weapons at the TO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, in response to the Prosecutor's question, you said that you did not remember who armed you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that now you remembered, now that you have read this statement, and is it true what you stated in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I stated in 1998 is true. And I would also like to say something else. I believe that everything that I saw and heard is not possible for me to express. I would need maybe three months for somebody to listen to me, and even then I wouldn't be able to tell everything. I think that there were five or six people there whose names I didn't know. I'm not very good with names. I'm suffering some consequences. I still can see quite far, and I hear very well. If necessary, I will explain how this came about. There were several people of Serbian nationality who were present when the weapons were being issued. One of them was called Durmusic. His father's name is Janko. He worked at the TO. The second one wasn't there. He was the commander of the TO. His name was Milos Bogdanovic. He's of Serb ethnicity, from the village of Skarici. He's not among the living any more. I wish he was, so that he could confirm that he was the commander. If you wanted me to tell you why I received the weapons from him, I thought that this was a multi-ethnic army; that the commander, the Serb -- was a Serb; that the second person who was issuing the weapons was a Serb; that the other man, Mato, who worked at Velepromet, was a Croat; [redacted] I was expecting this to be a multi-ethnic army and that we would be defending the town from the enemies, who would disrupt the life together in Bosanski Samac. However, this is something that I was disappointed about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. So on the 16th, you didn't know that the commander of the TO, the gentleman you mentioned just now, the Croat Mato, and Marko Bozanic -- Bozanovic - I apologise - and Alija Fitozovic, this is something that you didn't know on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that they were the commanders. As far as I was concerned, on the 16th, the commander was Milos Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During your examination-in-chief, you stated that on the night of the 17th of April, you left your house, with your rifle, and went to the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The centre" is a sort of general term. Could you give us a little more detail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The centre of town is where the green market is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is near the park; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is close in Samac. I don't know exactly what you mean. Perhaps some 50 metres away as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the park?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your testimony, you said that while you were standing there at that place with other people, the firing, the shooting, was getting closer to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that same page, you said the following in response to the Prosecutor's question: [In English] "Did you or any of the other men fire any shots in anger?" [Interpretation] Your answer was: [In English] "No. There was no firing out of anger or any kind of rage, and there was no shooting between the warring factions." [Interpretation] My question is: If the shooting was getting closer to you and you weren't shooting, who was actually shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, my fellow citizens, who happened to be at the entrance to the town. Many of them are no longer alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So this means that there was shooting between the warring sides; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I said, that there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, could you please tell me: You were a member of the SDA; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the party military unit of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't a member of the party military unit of the SDA, until the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a commander of the logistics or the supply squad of that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I heard about that, at the trial in the spring of 1993, at the court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I have the usher --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's the number 2 document. Would you please mark it for identification purposes. It's the -- [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What? Which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know in English. That's why that's the name of the document. Supply unit. Supply unit, yes. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What number is it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The ID number will be D24/2 ter, identification number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I'm a bit tired. MR. DI FAZIO: Can I just see the document briefly so that I can clarify it's the same one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, with pleasure. Yes. This is a document where there are the names and surnames of my fellow citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name at the beginning of the document under the item "Commander"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. [redacted]. This is my phone number. Had you asked me, I wouldn't have known it off by heart, but now I remember. This is the phone number that was never returned to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I just --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I asked very properly. I said: "Is it your name which appears as a commander on the top of that? Just answer yes or no." And the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We have that problem usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I mean, I really didn't anticipate that the witness will read the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Normally that happens, because of the flow of the evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm truly sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And depending on the area of cross-examination, maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm not -- I'm not -- this was just -- nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: One of -- okay. It's not necessary for private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. It's not necessary that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. The name will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, before the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see it at the military court in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't show it to me. However, in the material, I was charged as being the commander of the supply squad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it state at the very beginning of this document "supply squad"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that other people who are on this list are your fellow citizens and that you know them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, if you know, whether anyone else from this list was arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know either, believe me. Only if you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know most of my fellow citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any one of them was arrested? This is what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He was arrested together with me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please just read -- don't read the names, please. Just read the number.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 was with me for a long time, if we're thinking of the same person. Number 6 was with me for a long time. Number 8 was with me for a long time, and his father, who was born in 1911. I know the others, but I know them by name. So I'm afraid that I would make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher. Your Honours, thank you. I have finished my cross-examination. [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think at this stage we have a few matters to discuss before the other counsels can start cross-examination which, from the time, may not finish today. So the cross-examination will continue on Monday, from 0930 hours. And can the witness be led out of the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have to vacate the courtroom by 1.00 so that the equipment can be harnessed in for the meeting in the gallery this afternoon. I just have one item for the Prosecution which the Trial Chamber would like clarification on during the latter stages of your case with witnesses. The area is rather grey. Maybe it's too early in the Prosecution case. This is the issue of forced labour. From the evidence received so far and from the cross-examination, one can see that it's a very grey area. There were people who had assignments before the war, who had been in the military before, who had been informed that, "At any time when war is declared, you report to such-and-such a place for your work obligations during the war period." There were people who were not assigned like that, who were not -- who had not been in the military, either due to age or whatever reasons, but who were assigned work obligations when the war started in 1992. From some of the lists shown to the witnesses, there are names of professional people like doctors, for instance, health workers, for instance. Now, we have to clarify whether some of the professional people who had to work during wartime, after the war started in 1992, were working in the same institutions where they were working and were getting the same salaries that they were getting before the war but who were ordered never to leave, or whether the case was that even those who continued within their professions in the same institutions were not paid. And the other issue is whether or not in any of those categories of people who were made to work during the war, were they paid or not or was it a question of low wages for the labour. So these matters have to be clarified as you proceed with your witnesses, because it's quite a grey area to be able to determine what amounts to forced labour under the circumstances of this case. MR. DI FAZIO: The question of salaries and the question of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MR. DI FAZIO: The question of salaries and the question of professionals working in places like the hospital and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because we have the evidence that some lists were shown to witnesses that did say that these were doctors. They appear to have continued to work as doctors, as medical doctors during the -- after the war started, and is the question whether they were ordered never to leave their places of work, for instance, to leave Bosanski Samac altogether, to resign like any employee would do, and whether or not they continued receiving the same salaries or it was low wages or no salaries at all. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For instance, this witness still on the stand did say -- he did explain where he was working before the war. He did say he was supposed -- it was something like he was supposed to go back to work at that station after the war started, but he explained. So even though he was given other assignments, did the company where he was supposed to continue working, where he had been working before, pay anything to him, recognising the work that he was assigned to do after the war started. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: These areas need to be clarified during the further evidence that may be eliciting from your witnesses, because in other trials, it is quite a grey area as to what amounts to forced labour -- MR. DI FAZIO: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- when an indictment is drawn the way this one is drawn. MR. DI FAZIO: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand the concerns --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- and I will make sure that the witnesses -- that we proof the witnesses on these issues and we get every bit of evidence that might be useful to the Chamber in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Just thinking off the top of my head, one of the witnesses that we deleted from our list was, in fact, a doctor who worked in Bosanski Samac. May I just very briefly confer with my colleague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You'll deal with that. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll deal with the issue that you have raised. Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber was informed that Mr. Pantelic wanted to raise some issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Very briefly. During these proceedings, I think that we established -- we have a well-established practice about this swapping the place of our defendants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The accused, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, the court officer -- well, court policeman here was in charge, like a superior to the unit of yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- by his own initiative made another position of the defendants which might be a problem for the future. So the issue is whether we are following your instruction here or instruction of this particular person. If -- the bottom line is if the interference in this situation will occur in future, then we shall be in situation to lose and not to know what the previous position was, because my understanding was that for each particular witness, we have the same position of the defendants, and then for the next witness, the next position. If it will be -- changes during the examination of one witness, then it will -- we shall be bring into the situation where we shall not follow the standards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. If --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean, I'm very sorry. I said to my learned colleague here not to raise this to the Trial Chamber, but they told me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The position was that, and the position is still that -- for each witness, before a new witness comes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- the defendants change positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And if we have two days of examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They retain those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's illogical to change for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. They retain the same positions until we finish -- before the next witness comes, they again vary their positions, retain those positions and up to the end of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I hope Ms. Registrar will inform, although I have very nice relations with all the officers, and they are very kind and very professional, still but, you know, there are some persons who think that my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.
